note: Every bundled dataset is watched by a refresh adapter, by the change-watch
(scripts/refresh/source-watch.json), or it is listed here with the reason it is
not. Nothing may be unwatched silently.
This list exists because on 2026-08-30 nobody could say which shards were
covered. Twenty-three of eighty were not, and the count was not written down
anywhere -- the adapter check reports on the adapters that exist, never on the
shards that have none, so a dataset with no adapter is invisible to the one
report that would say so.
The list should SHRINK. An id here is a shard whose figures nothing is
checking, sitting behind a citation that still looks live -- the failure this
whole pipeline was built to prevent. Five of these cite the very revenue
procedure the federal income-tax adapter already fetches and parses every
month.
A reason is a decision someone can argue with later, not a shrug. 'Nothing to
parse' has to say why.
gift-tax-2024 came off this list on 2026-08-30, the day the list was written --
which is the point of it. Four shards still cite rp-25-32.pdf with no adapter.
Two reasons here were wrong when this list was first written on 2026-08-30, in
opposite directions, and both were corrected the same day. savers-credit was
described as stated on a web page: its caps are in Notice 2025-67, which the
pipeline fetches, and it now has an adapter. education-credits was described as
indexing: § 25A(i) fixed its phase-out ranges and they have not moved.
That is worth leaving in the note rather than quietly editing away. A reason is
a claim like any other, and a list of unchecked claims about why things are not
checked is the last place anyone would think to look for an error.

unwatched.aca-2024: Its applicable-percentage table comes from its own annual revenue procedure (rp-25-25.pdf), reissued at a new URL each year, so an adapter pointed at this one would be reading a closed document that reports agreement forever. It wants a watch on whatever page lists the current procedure, which has not been found yet.
unwatched.rmd-uniform-lifetime-2024: The Uniform Lifetime Table is a regulation, not an indexed figure: Treasury last reissued it for 2022 and it moves only when the mortality assumptions are revised. Pub 590-B restates it. A change is a rulemaking somebody reads, so this belongs on the change-watch rather than under an adapter, and has not been added yet.
unwatched.education-credits-2024: The AOTC and Lifetime Learning phase-out ranges are STATUTORY and do not index: § 25A(i) fixed them at $80,000-$90,000 (single) and $160,000-$180,000 (joint), and the 2020 Act aligned the Lifetime Learning range to the same figures rather than continuing to adjust it. So there is no annual figure for an adapter to chase and the inflation-adjustment procedure states none — a change is an act of Congress. This is Delaware's shape and belongs on the change-watch, which wants a fetchable statutory source that has not been found yet.
unwatched.social-security-2024: The full-retirement-age schedule is statutory (42 U.S.C. 416(l)) and keyed to year of birth, so it does not index and has not moved since the 1983 amendments. The figures that DO move annually -- the wage base and the COLA -- live in fica-2024, which the SSA adapter watches.
unwatched.social-security-taxation-2024: The $25,000 / $32,000 provisional-income thresholds are statutory and were deliberately never indexed: they have not moved since 1983 and 1993 respectively, which is why an ever-growing share of benefits is taxable. There is no annual figure to chase, so this belongs on the change-watch beside Delaware.
unwatched.fafsa-2024-2025: The SAI formula tables are reissued annually in the ED SAI Formula Guide, a PDF at a new path each award year, so an adapter pointed at this one would report agreement forever. It wants a watch on the Knowledge Center page that lists the current guide.
